original_question: For each positive integer e, let S(e) be the supremum of rho(Gamma) over all symmetric numerical semigroups Gamma with embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = e, where a numerical semigroup is symmetric when for every integer x not in Gamma one has Frob(Gamma) - x in Gamma. Determine S(e).
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 16 (the extremal number of relations for symmetric numerical semigroups of fixed embedding dimension), with Problem 17 giving the finiteness subquestion known as Bresinsky’s problem.
correct_elements: You correctly fix the embedding dimension e, restrict to symmetric numerical semigroups, and ask for the extremal value of rho(Gamma). That is the right problem from the paper: Section 4 asks for the maximal possible number of relations of a symmetric numerical semigroup with given embedding dimension. Your symmetry condition is equivalent to the paper’s notion of a symmetric numerical semigroup.
missing_details: The paper’s rho(Gamma) must be defined: it is the cardinality of a minimal presentation of Gamma, i.e. the number of minimal relations among the minimal generators of Gamma.
The ambient object should be made explicit: a numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of N = {0,1,2,...}.
The embedding dimension should be defined as the cardinality of the unique minimal generating set of Gamma.
The extremum should be understood as taken in N union {infinity}; the paper immediately isolates the question whether this supremum is finite for every e as a separate open problem (Problem 17).

To be fully paper-faithful, one should note the equivalent characterizations of symmetry used nearby in the paper: Gamma is symmetric iff t(Gamma)=1, equivalently iff its semigroup ring is Gorenstein.
If one uses the ring-theoretic equivalent formulation, one should specify that k is an arbitrary field and that rho(Gamma)=beta_1(k[[Gamma]])=beta_1(k[t^Gamma]).
refined_question: For each positive integer e, let S_sym(e) := sup{ rho(Gamma) : Gamma is a symmetric numerical semigroup with edim(Gamma)=e }, where rho(Gamma) denotes the cardinality of a minimal presentation of Gamma (equivalently, the number of minimal relations among the minimal generators of Gamma), edim(Gamma) is the cardinality of the unique minimal generating set of Gamma, and a numerical semigroup Gamma is symmetric if for every integer x not in Gamma one has Frob(Gamma)-x in Gamma. Determine S_sym(e) for all e; in particular, is S_sym(e) finite for every e?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for each positive integer e, determine sup{ beta_1(k[[Gamma]]) : Gamma is a numerical semigroup with edim(Gamma)=e and k[[Gamma]] is Gorenstein }, where k is any field.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s target. Section 1 defines rho(Gamma) as the cardinality of a minimal presentation and identifies it with the first Betti number of the semigroup ring. Section 4 then defines symmetric numerical semigroups and states the fixed-embedding-dimension extremal question in exactly this form as Problem 16. The same section immediately singles out the finiteness issue as Problem 17 (Bresinsky’s problem), and records the main nearby evidence in Theorem 11 (the embedding-dimension-4 case) and Theorem 12 (a sharp partial bound in embedding dimension 5).
